content: Dual specificity protein phosphatase 1 (DUSP1) is an enzyme encoded by the DUSP1 gene in humans. Function The expression of the DUSP1 gene is upregulated in human skin fibroblasts in response to oxidative stress, heat stress, and growth factors. The protein encoded by this gene exhibits structural characteristics similar to those found in the non-receptor-type protein-tyrosine phosphatase family. Additionally, it shares significant amino acid sequence similarity with a Tyr/Ser-protein phosphatase encoded by the late gene H1 of the vaccinia virus. The DUSP1 protein, when expressed and purified in bacterial systems, demonstrates intrinsic phosphatase activity. It specifically inactivates mitogen-activated protein (MAP) kinase in vitro by simultaneously dephosphorylating both its phosphothreonine and phosphotyrosine residues. Furthermore, DUSP1 suppresses the activation of MAP kinase by oncogenic Ras in extracts derived from Xenopus oocytes. These findings suggest that DUSP1 plays a critical role in the human cellular response to environmental stress and in the negative regulation of cellular proliferation. Interactions DUSP1 has been shown to interact with MAPK14, MAPK1, and MAPK8.
